subject: RetailNova API latency & 502s — network path investigation
messages:
From: David Gomez <david.gomez@retailnova.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@retailnova.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: RetailNova: sudden API latency & 502s impacting checkout

Priya,

We started seeing a sharp increase in API latency and intermittent 502s hitting our checkout flows around 08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6% and p95 latency climbed from ~120ms to >1.3s. Impact is visible across us-west-2 nodes only.

Attached is a small packet capture around 08:48 where you can see repeated TCP retransmits and a handful of TTL exceeded responses that look like asymmetric routing. We believe traffic to Redwood endpoints is intermittently taking a different egress/peer path and timing out.

Customer impact: two major retail customers have started seeing checkout failures and abandoned carts are climbing. We need confirmation that this is on your side and an estimated mitigation ETA.

Attachements: [Attachment: packet-capture-20280611.pcap (pcap), ~3MB]

-David
David Gomez

On Tue, Jun 11, 2028 at 09:23 AM David Gomez <david.gomez@retailnova.com> wrote:
> Priya,
>
> We started seeing a sharp increase in API latency and intermittent 502s hitting our checkout flows around 08:45 PDT...

Quick triage notes (nets/infra):
- We’re seeing transient route withdraws on the peering session to RetailNova’s ASN in us-west-2 between 08:42–08:50. BGP updates show flaps that correlate with the spike window.
- DNS: our edge resolvers in us-west-2 returned a small batch of SERVFAILs at 08:49 for the partner resolver set; this appears correlated with the route instability.
- Observed TCP retransmits and a handful of duplicate acks in the pcap — consistent with a path that is dropping or experiencing MTU/fragmentation issues mid-hop.
- There’s a third-party transit (CloudMesh) in the path for a subset of customers; we see increased latency on that path.

Temporary mitigations applied (09:40):
- We pushed a conservative routing preference to avoid the affected peer for RetailNova prefixes in us-west-2.
- Increased edge resolver caching TTL for the affected route to blunt DNS jitter.
- Spin up a hot standby pool in a separate AZ and routed a percentage of RetailNova traffic to it (canary).

Next steps:
1) Karthik — can you coordinate with CloudMesh (Alex) to confirm whether they had a maintenance window or transient hardware issue?
2) Sean — please prepare a short exec note for RetailNova (we should offer a one-time credit and timeline).
3) Priya — I’ll prepare packet-level artifacts and a short runbook for mitigation steps.

Attachments: [Attachment: network-runbook.pdf (docx/pdf) — initial triage steps and rollback guide]

Marissa Cole
Lead Infrastructure Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — we still see intermittent 502s for ~12% of requests hitting the us-west-2 fleet (sampled metrics at 10:00). The temporary reroute reduced errors for ~60% of traffic but the problem persists for specific CIDR ranges.

Impact is material: two enterprise customers reported checkout errors for ~18 minutes each and are requesting an executive update and details on what happened. Please include packet traces and the remediation timeline — they’ve asked about SLA credits.

Alex (CloudMesh) — can you confirm if there were any fiber reroutes or maintenance in us-west-2 during 08:40–09:00?

-David
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: David Gomez <david.gomez@retailnova.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: RetailNova — executive summary & action plan (post incident)

David — short executive summary and next steps after the event on Jun 11 (08:42–09:02 PDT):

Summary:
- Root cause: transient peering route instability on a third-party transit (CloudMesh) in us-west-2 that caused asymmetric paths and intermittent packet loss between RetailNova and Redwood egress nodes. Concurrently, a small portion of our edge resolvers returned SERVFAILs that amplified error rates.
- Customer impact: p95 latency increased to >1.3s and 502 rate peaked at ~12% for affected prefixes; two enterprise customers experienced checkout failures for ~18 minutes each.

Action taken (completed):
- Immediate routing preference change to avoid the affected CloudMesh path for RetailNova prefixes (reduced errors by ~60%).
- Increased edge resolver caching and rolled a canary to a hot-standby AZ.
- Packet captures and runbook artifacts collected and attached.

Planned longer-term remediation (next 72 hours):
1) Joint postmortem with CloudMesh to confirm root cause and commit to RFO and preventative steps. (Karthik to coordinate — target: 24h)
2) Add route dampening and stricter BGP health checks for retail customer prefixes in us-west-2. (Marissa to lead — target: 48h)
3) Harden DNS resolver upstreams and add an additional redundancy layer for retail-critical routes. (Infra + DNS team — target: 72h)
4) Offer RetailNova a one-time service credit for the outage window and a technical debrief with their SREs. (Sean to coordinate customer comms and credit).

Attachments: [Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (xlsx), Attachment: network-runbook.pdf (pdf), Attachment: packet-capture-20280611.pcap (pcap)]

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min technical debrief with our infra leads and CloudMesh tomorrow. Please let me know preferred times.

—Priya
